data.text: [00:00]CD1 Track 38
M = Martin, T = Tina
[00:04]It’s great to be back … We’ve got so much catching up to do!
[00:09]Yeah, there’s so much to tell you! I know, I’ll show you some photos from my birthday party.
[00:16.3]Oh, that’s a good idea … I can see who your friends are.

[00:20]Yes, I had a bit of a party with some of my best … you know, my closest friends. `[00:27]We had a lovely time. Let’s see … where are they? `[00:33]OK … here we are … this is a good one. So, well, first, this is Alison.
[00:40.6]Mmm … yes, I think I remember her …

[00:43.5]Yes, I’ve known Alison for years. `[00:47]I mean, we’re old school friends – from primary school – so, I suppose I’ve known her nearly all my life really. `[00:56]We first met when we were in the same class at school from the age of four and a half.
[01:01.6]Four and a half? Really?

[01:03.8]Yeah, even when we were at school together, we never fell out with each other about anything. `[01:10]She’s a very easy-going person and still a really great friend. `[01:15]I’m very glad we’ve kept in touch. `[01:18]I suppose we see each other about once a month and we still get on really well.
[01:24.2]Mmm, that’s really nice. And who’s that? He looks like a bit of a character!

[01:31]Yes! He’s great … That’s my friend Jake. `[01:35.9]Basically, I go to the gym with him! `[01:39]Actually, he was a colleague first. `[01:42]I got to know him at work and we’ve worked together for about five years now. `[01:48]Then, about a year ago, we started going to the gym together. `[01:52.9]It’s really good because we help each other to keep motivated.
[01:57.5]I need a friend like that!

[01:59]Well, that’s right. `[02:01]It’s hard to keep going to the gym and exercising on your own, isn’t it? `[02:06]Because I’ve got someone to go with, it’s much easier. He’s always encouraging me, and motivating me. `[02:10]I think he feels the same, too. `[02:17]So, yes, we see each other at work, and we go to the gym together … and I would definitely say he’s a really good friend.
[02:26.4]Yes …
[02:27]Oh, … and Melanie. That’s her … She’s a lovely friend – always there for me. `[02:35]I met her at a party, actually – about ten years ago … but then we lost touch for a while.
[02:41.7]Oh, really?

[02:42.7]Well, yes, but a couple of years ago, we met again and we’ve been really close since then. `[02:49]I call her my ‘three o’clock in the morning’ friend because she really is the kind of person who you can phone up at three o’clock in the morning if you need to, and she really wouldn’t mind.
[03:00]That’s great …

[03:01.9]In fact, I have phoned her at that time on a couple of occasions. `[03:06]You know, when I’ve been really down about something and really needed someone to talk to. I see her at least once a week. `[03:15]She’s my best friend … she really is … `[03:18]She’s a very special person – she doesn’t give you advice, you know. She just listens. It’s a great quality in a friend, I think.
[03:28.7]Yes, definitely … Oh, who’s that? I think I recognise him …
